| API-3 | Rendering is machine- and configuration-independent: no reliance on float formatting, `sys.set_int_max_str_digits` limits beyond the interpreter default, or platform-specific conversion. | FR-201 |
| API-4 | Output length scales linearly to the operand digit count (per NFR-2); no truncation and no ellipsis for very large results. | FR-201 |

### F-10: Usage/help output
| id | Contract | Trace |
|---|---|---|
| API-1 | The canonical usage line is emitted to **stderr** whenever the arity rule is violated (the F-1/F-5 trigger). | FR-226 |
| API-2 | The usage line is a fixed literal: no runtime interpolation of operands, environment, or paths; byte-identical across all runs and hosts. | FR-226 |
| API-3 | The usage line is emitted exactly once per failing run and always terminates with a single `\n`. | FR-226 |
| API-4 | No flag path exists: the program does not accept `-h`/`--help` and never emits usage on stdout. | FR-226, FR-1 |
| API-5 | The usage line is not localized — English-only, ASCII, locale-independent. | FR-226 |

### F-11: Unit tests for the add function and CLI
| id | Contract | Trace |
|---|---|---|
| API-1 | Test entry surface: the suite is runnable from the project root via `python -m unittest` or `python -m unittest discover` on stock CPython 3.8+ with no third-party packages. | FR-252 |
| API-2 | In-process call tests target `add(a, b)` directly and assert exact `int` equality on the returned value. | FR-251 |
| API-3 | CLI tests invoke the shipped entry point as a subprocess and assert the triple `(stdout_bytes, stderr_bytes, exit_status)` against the F-4/F-5 contracts. | FR-251 |
| API-4 | Tests are hermetic: no network, no external fixtures, no build/install step; fixtures are generated in-test from the F-2 grammar. | FR-252 |
| API-5 | The suite asserts the cross-feature invariants: status `0` ⟺ exactly one stdout line and empty stderr; status `2` ⟺ empty stdout and non-empty stderr. | FR-253 |

## 1. Design Direction

`add` is a zero-chrome command-line utility, so its entire "visual language" is the byte stream it produces and the ergonomics of typing it. The design direction is therefore **radically minimal, deterministic, and composable**: the ideal invocation is the shortest one that can exist (`add 2 3`), the success output is a single base-10 line on stdout, and every failure is a single diagnosable event on stderr with a stable exit status. There is no TUI, no color, no spinner, no prompt, and no state — the utility must feel like a POSIX primitive that a shell script can depend on for a decade.

Mood: **quiet, exact, and unsurprising.** The tool should disappear. Nothing about its behaviour — argument handling (F-1, F-2), arithmetic (F-3), rendering (F-4, F-8, F-9), exit status (F-5), diagnostics (F-6, F-10), or dependency envelope (F-7) — may vary run to run, machine to machine, or locale to locale. A user should be able to predict byte-for-byte what `add` will emit for any given argument vector without running it.

Visual language (in the CLI sense): **one line in, one line out, ASCII only.** The canonical shapes are `add <int1> <int2>` for invocation, `<sum>\n` for success, and `<error>\n<usage>\n` (or the F-6/F-10-specified diagnostic pair) for failure. Signs are ASCII `+`/`-` (F-2, F-8), digits are ASCII `0`–`9`, the terminator is exactly one `\n` (U+000A), and no radix prefix, thousands separator, leading zero, ANSI escape, or Unicode glyph ever appears in machine-readable output. stdout is reserved exclusively for the result (F-4); stderr is reserved exclusively for diagnostics and usage (F-6, F-10); the two streams never cross-contaminate.

Priority of experience values, highest first: **correctness and determinism** (arbitrary-precision, sign-exact, locale-proof — F-3, F-8, F-9) → **composability and scriptability** (clean stdout, meaningful exit codes, no flags, no interactive behaviour — F-1, F-4, F-5) → **diagnosability** (the offending argument is named, the expected usage is shown, the failure is one line — F-6, F-10) → **zero-friction install and run** (stock CPython 3.9+, no third-party packages, no build step — F-7) → **verifiable behaviour** (the full contract is exercised by the stdlib `unittest` suite required by F-11). Anything that would trade away a higher-priority value for a lower-priority one — for example, adding a colored error message that pollutes stderr or depends on a third-party package — is out of direction for this project.

The single design non-negotiable that follows from this direction: **the observable interface of `add` — stdout bytes, stderr bytes, and exit status — is a contract, not a presentation.** Every downstream feature (F-1 … F-10) and every test (F-11) is designed against that contract, and no feature may widen it, soften it, or make it conditional on environment, TTY-ness, locale, or user configuration.

*(This section describes the interface direction only. Concrete module layout, entry-point mechanism, packaging, and interpreter-version targeting are decided by the Architect agent in `docs/architecture.md`; concrete literal error/usage strings are fixed by F-6 and F-10.)*

## Components

### Component-model overview
`add` is a single-process, single-threaded, dependency-free Python 3 CLI. It is decomposed below into the smallest units that each own exactly one externally-observable obligation from the spec. Three tiers are used: **primitives** (single concern, no orchestration), **composed** components (they sequence primitives into a path), and **feature components** (the named surfaces `F-1 … F-11` that other agents and the traceability matrix link to). Nothing here introduces a technology choice; the units are logical and language-neutral, and F-7 constrains them to be realisable with the Python 3 standard library alone.

### Component inventory

| Component | Tier | Single responsibility | Feature anchor | Requirement anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ArgvReader | primitive | Read the process argument vector, discard `argv[0]`, hand the remaining token list onward unmodified. Performs no interpretation. | F-1, F-2 | FR-1, FR-26 |
| ArityGate | primitive | Assert that the token list holds exactly two operands; short-circuit to the failure path otherwise. | F-1, F-5, F-6 | FR-6, FR-101, FR-102, FR-126 |
| GrammarValidator | primitive | Decide accept/reject for one operand against the F-2 decimal-integer grammar; never mutates the token. | F-2, F-6 | FR-27 … FR-32, FR-127 |
| IntegerParser | primitive | Convert an already-validated token into an exact arbitrary-precision integer value; never sees unpalatable input. | F-2, F-3 | FR-52, FR-53 |
| BigIntAdder | primitive | Produce the exact mathematical sum of the two parsed operands. Pure function of its two inputs. | F-3, F-8, F-9 | FR-51, FR-52, FR-54, FR-55 |
| DecimalRenderer | primitive | Render an integer value as a canonical base-10 ASCII digit string, with a leading `-` iff the value is strictly negative and no other glyph. | F-4, F-8, F-9 | FR-76 … FR-79, FR-176, FR-177, FR-201, FR-202 |
| LineEmitter | primitive | Write exactly one supplied string followed by exactly one `\n` (U+000A) to stdout; flushes before exit. | F-4 | FR-78 |
| ErrEmitter | primitive | Write a supplied diagnostic string (or the usage line) to stderr, one line at a time; never touches stdout. | F-6, F-10 | FR-127, FR-226 |
| ExitController | primitive | Set the process exit status to the value dictated by the terminal outcome; the only component that calls the exit mechanism. | F-5 | FR-101, FR-102, FR-103 |
| DiagnosticCatalogue | primitive | Hold the exact literal texts (arity error, grammar error naming the offending argument) and produce them from the failing stage’s data. No runtime interpolation beyond the offending token. | F-6 | FR-127 |
| UsageTextProvider | primitive | Hold the canonical usage line as a compile-time literal, emitted verbatim. | F-10 | FR-226 |
| StdlibGuard | primitive | Ensure no non-stdlib import, no network use, and no installation step is reachable from any other component. Asserted statically at import time. | F-7 | FR-151, FR-152 |

### Composed components

| Component | Composes | Ordering | Feature anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| SuccessPath | ArgvReader → ArityGate(pass) → GrammarValidator(operand 1, pass) → GrammarValidator(operand 2, pass) → IntegerParser(×2) → BigIntAdder → DecimalRenderer → LineEmitter → ExitController(0) | Fixed; no stage may be skipped, reordered, or re-run. | F-1, F-2, F-3, F-4, F-5 |
| FailurePath | ArgvReader → (ArityGate fail ⌄ GrammarValidator fail) → DiagnosticCatalogue → ErrEmitter → UsageTextProvider → ErrEmitter → ExitController(2) | The first failing stage aborts the pipeline; later stages MUST NOT run. stdout is never written on this path. | F-1, F-5, F-6, F-10 |
| ValidationOrchestrator | ArityGate → GrammarValidator(×2) with fail-fast semantics and stream discipline | Deterministic check order owned by F-6; the grammar itself is owned by F-2. | F-6 |

### Feature components (one per product-plan feature)

| Feature component | Disposition | Backing primitives | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-1** `add` command entry point | Composed facade | ArgvReader, SuccessPath, FailurePath | Owns the invocable surface and the parse → add → render → emit sequence; re-defines nothing downstream. |
| **F-2** Two positional integer operands | Primitive | GrammarValidator, IntegerParser | Owns accept/reject of a token; sign placement, leading zeros, and forbidden characters are its rules alone. |
| **F-3** Integer addition | Primitive | BigIntAdder | Pure; sign law and additive identity are its only rules. |
| **F-4** Print result to stdout | Primitive | DecimalRenderer, LineEmitter | Owns the stdout envelope: base 10, ASCII digits, one trailing `\n`, no leading zeros. |
| **F-5** Exit-status contract | Primitive | ExitController | Owns the numeric status; asserts the invariants linking status to the two byte streams. |
| **F-6** Input validation and error message | Composed | ValidationOrchestrator, DiagnosticCatalogue, ErrEmitter | Owns check ordering, exact message text, safe echoing, and the empty-stdout-on-failure invariant. |
| **F-7** Standard library only | Primitive | StdlibGuard | Owns the dependency envelope; no component may import outside the stdlib. |
| **F-8** Correct handling of negative results | Primitive | DecimalRenderer | Owns the strictly-negative branch of rendering: ASCII `-` U+002D only, no Unicode look-alikes. |
| **F-9** Arbitrary-precision output | Primitive | DecimalRenderer | Owns the scale envelope: exact digit count, no fixed-width cap, locale-independent digits. |
| **F-10** Usage/help output | Primitive | UsageTextProvider, ErrEmitter | Owns the usage literal, its channel, its emission count, and its terminators. |
| **F-11** Unit tests for the `add` function and CLI | Test suite | see Test components | Owns automated verification of F-1 … F-10; does not redefine their behaviour. |

### Data model

`DM-` ids below are the shape-only carriers exchanged between components. They carry no serialized form, no persistence, and no wire format — the program has no I/O beyond the two byte streams.

| Id | Name | Shape (logical) | Produced by | Consumed by | Feature anchor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DM-1 | ArgumentVector | ordered list of raw argument strings, `argv[0]` excluded | ArgvReader | ArityGate, GrammarValidator | F-1, F-2 |
| DM-2 | OperandToken | a single raw string, position 1 or 2 | ArgumentVector projection | GrammarValidator | F-2 |
| DM-3 | ParsedOperand | exact integer value + its source token (for diagnostics) | IntegerParser | BigIntAdder | F-2, F-3 |
| DM-4 | SumValue | exact integer value | BigIntAdder | DecimalRenderer | F-3 |
| DM-5 | RenderedLine | canonical ASCII string with no terminator | DecimalRenderer | LineEmitter | F-4, F-8, F-9 |
| DM-6 | Diagnostic | exact literal line text + channel (stderr) | DiagnosticCatalogue, UsageTextProvider | ErrEmitter | F-6, F-10 |
| DM-7 | ExitOutcome | one of `{success:0, usage-error:2, grammar-error:2}` | SuccessPath, FailurePath | ExitController | F-5 |

### Test components

| Id | Test unit | Asserts | Feature anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| T-1 | `add()` function unit tests | Arithmetic exactness across representative operands (F-3). | F-11, F-3 |
| T-2 | CLI end-to-end tests (subprocess) | stdout bytes, stderr bytes, and exit status for a fixed invocation table. | F-11, F-1, F-4, F-5 |
| T-3 | Grammar table tests | Accept/reject parity with the F-2 grammar for a broad corpus (signs, leading zeros, whitespace, underscores, decimals, commas, exponents, base prefixes, stray signs). | F-11, F-2 |
| T-4 | Sign and zero tests | Emitted `-` is U+002D only; zero renders as `0`; positive sums carry no `+`. | F-11, F-4, F-8 |
| T-5 | Arbitrary-precision tests | Digit-count equality against generated large operands; no width cap. | F-11, F-9 |
| T-6 | Exit-status tests | Status is `0` on success and `2` on every failure category, with the stream invariants of F-5. | F-11, F-5 |
| T-7 | Stream-separation tests | Zero stdout bytes on any failure; zero stderr bytes on success. | F-11, F-1, F-4, F-6 |
| T-8 | Stdlib-only test | No non-stdlib import is reachable; suite runs with `python -m unittest` and no network. | F-11, F-7 |
| T-9 | Usage-text test | The usage line is the F-10 literal, is emitted to stderr, and appears exactly once per failing run. | F-11, F-10 |

### Component interaction

**Success flow (F-1 → F-2 → F-3 → F-4 → F-5):**
`ArgvReader` → DM-1 → `ArityGate` (pass) → `GrammarValidator` ×2 (accept) → `IntegerParser` ×2 → DM-3 ×2 → `BigIntAdder` → DM-4 → `DecimalRenderer` → DM-5 → `LineEmitter` (stdout, one `\n`) → `ExitController(0)`. `ErrEmitter` is never invoked and stdout receives exactly one line.

**Failure flow (F-1 → F-2/F-6 → F-5):**
`ArgvReader` → DM-1 → `ValidationOrchestrator` detects the first failing stage (arity, operand 1 grammar, or operand 2 grammar) and aborts. `DiagnosticCatalogue` yields DM-6 (error line), then `UsageTextProvider` yields DM-6 (usage line); `ErrEmitter` writes both to stderr; stdout receives zero bytes; `ExitController(2)`. `BigIntAdder`, `DecimalRenderer`, and `LineEmitter` are never reached.

**Purity and boundary invariants:**
`BigIntAdder` is a pure function of DM-3 ×2 and has no knowledge of argv, streams, or status. `DecimalRenderer` is a pure function of DM-4 and has no knowledge of the operand tokens. `ExitController` is the only component that terminates the process. `ErrEmitter` and `LineEmitter` do not share state; neither can write to the other’s channel. `StdlibGuard` is asserted at import time and must hold before any path runs.

### Open Questions
*(None for the component breakdown. Where the spec is silent — e.g. the exact literal of the F-6 diagnostic line and the F-10 usage line — those literals are owned by the corresponding feature sections and are not decided here; the components reference them by name so no text is re-invented in this section.)*

## Data Models

**Scope.** This section defines the logical data models for `add`. `add` is **stateless and file-free**: it opens no database, writes no file, holds no session, and emits no serialized document. Every model below is therefore either (a) an in-memory value whose lifetime is a single process run, or (b) a compile-time constant with process-wide lifetime. Ids `DM-1` … `DM-11` are defined once, here, and are never re-defined elsewhere. Types are language-neutral; F-7 (`FR-151`, `FR-152`) constrains every model to be realisable with the Python 3 standard library alone.

**Non-goals.** No persistence layer, no schema/migration model, no wire/serialization format, no configuration model (no env vars, no config file — `FR-152`), no i18n resource model (F-10 forbids localization of the usage text; F-4/F-9 forbid locale-dependent rendering), and no user/identity model (there is no user concept in this product).

### Conventions

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Cardinality `1` | Exactly one value, always present |
| Cardinality `0..1` | Optional; absent is a distinct, meaningful state |
| Cardinality `0..*` | Ordered list; order is significant |
| Invariant | Condition that must hold at all times; violation is a defect, not an error path |
| ASCII | U+0000 – U+007F inclusive |
| Canonical digits | The string `0`, or `[1-9][0-9]*` — no leading zeros (`FR-79`, `FR-202`) |
| Constant | Model is fixed for the whole process; not reachable by argv, env, locale, or config |

### DM-1: `Invocation` — the per-process aggregate

The single top-level record for one execution. Everything else is either owned by it or derived from it.

| Field | Type | Card. | Constraints | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `program_name` | str | 1 | Verbatim `argv[0]`; never interpreted as an operand | `FR-1` |
| `raw_args` | str[] | 0..* | Verbatim OS tokens following `program_name`; no re-tokenization, no shell re-splitting, no option parsing | `FR-1`, `FR-26`, `FR-27` |
| `arity_ok` | bool | 1 | `True` iff `len(raw_args) == 2` | `FR-6`, `FR-102`, `FR-126` |
| `operands` | `ParsedOperand[2]` | 0..2 | Present only when `arity_ok`; element order is positional (`DM-3.slot` 1 then 2) | `FR-26`, `FR-126` |
| `sum` | `Sum` | 0..1 | Present only when both operands are `accepted` | `FR-3`, `FR-51` |
| `stdout_record` | `OutputEnvelope` | 0..1 | Present iff `outcome == SUCCESS` | `FR-4`, `FR-76` |
| `diagnostics` | `DiagnosticMessage[]` | 0..* | Non-empty iff `outcome != SUCCESS`; never emitted to stdout | `FR-6`, `FR-7`, `FR-127` |
| `usage_emitted` | bool | 1 | `True` iff the `DM-8` literal was written to stderr | `FR-226` |
| `outcome` | enum `Outcome` | 1 | Exactly one of `SUCCESS`, `ARITY_ERROR`, `GRAMMAR_ERROR` | `FR-101`–`FR-104` |
| `exit_status` | `ExitStatus` | 1 | Derived from `outcome` via `DM-7`; never set independently | `FR-101`, `FR-102`, `FR-103` |

**Invariants**

- `len(raw_args) == len(operand_tokens)` — no token is added, dropped, reordered, or rewritten.
- `outcome == SUCCESS` ⟹ `arity_ok` and both `operands[i].accepted` and `stdout_record` present and `diagnostics` empty.
- `outcome != SUCCESS` ⟹ `stdout_record` absent **and** `DiagnosticMessage` count ≥ 1 (`FR-127`'s zero-stdout-bytes rule).
- Stream disjointness: `stdout_record` and `diagnostics` are never both non-empty.
- Terminal state: once `exit_status` is fixed, no field may mutate. There is no post-exit mutation path.
- `program_name` never flows into `operands`.

**Lifecycle / state transitions**

| Id | From | Trigger | To | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `T-1` | `START` | process begins | `READ_ARGV` | populate `program_name`, `raw_args`; discard `program_name` |
| `T-2` | `READ_ARGV` | `len(raw_args) != 2` | `ARITY_ERROR` | emit arity `DiagnosticMessage` + `DM-8` usage line; `exit_status = 2` |
| `T-3` | `READ_ARGV` | `len(raw_args) == 2` | `VALIDATE_OPERAND_1` | validate `raw_args[0]` against `DM-2` |
| `T-4` | `VALIDATE_OPERAND_1` | reject | `GRAMMAR_ERROR` | emit grammar `DiagnosticMessage`; `exit_status = 2` |
| `T-5` | `VALIDATE_OPERAND_1` | accept | `VALIDATE_OPERAND_2` | validate `raw_args[1]` (never runs after a stage-1 failure — `FR-126`) |
| `T-6` | `VALIDATE_OPERAND_2` | reject | `GRAMMAR_ERROR` | as `T-4` |
| `T-7` | `VALIDATE_OPERAND_2` | accept | `COMPUTE` | build `DM-4` |
| `T-8` | `COMPUTE` | sum computed | `RENDER` | build `DM-5` |
| `T-9` | `RENDER` | line fully written to stdout | `EXIT_SUCCESS` | `exit_status = 0` |

`T-2`, `T-4`, `T-6`, `T-9` are absorbing. The pipeline is strictly linear and single-pass: no retries, no fallback, no interactive prompt, no subsequent stage after the first failure (`FR-126`).

### DM-2: `DecimalIntegerGrammar` — the operand language (constant)

A static, immutable description of the accepted operand token language. Not parameterised at runtime.

| Field | Value / Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `grammar_id` | `"DEC10"` | Stable identifier for traceability |
| `pattern` | `[+-]?[0-9]+` | Canonical form: optional single sign, one or more ASCII digits |
| `sign_chars` | `{U+002B "+", U+002D "-"}` | Sign permitted **only** at index 0 |
| `digit_class` | `U+0030`–`U+0039` | ASCII decimal only; no Unicode digit category |
| `min_digits_after_sign` | `1` | A bare sign (`"+"`, `"-"`) is rejected — `FR-32` |
| `leading_zeros` | allowed | `007`, `-000`, `+00042` accepted and interpreted base-10 (`FR-28`) |
| `forbidden_substrings` | whitespace, `_`, `.`, `,`, `e`/`E`, `0x`, `0o`, `0b` | `FR-31` |
| `forbidden_chars` | any char outside `digit_class ∪ sign_chars` | Includes U+2212 MINUS SIGN, U+00A0, thousands separators, fullwidth digits |
| `locale_sensitive` | `false` | Grammar is fixed regardless of `LANG`/`LC_*` |
| `configurable` | `false` | No env var, flag, or file can alter it (`FR-152`) |

**Invariants**

- Deterministic: the accept/reject decision for a given token is identical on every run, machine, and locale.
- Sign position is strictly index 0; a sign at any later index is rejected (it falls outside `digit_class`).
- Empty string is rejected (fails `min_digits_after_sign`).
- Emptiness, sign-only, and out-of-class characters are rejected — never coerced, trimmed, or repaired. There is no "best effort" parse.

### DM-3: `ParsedOperand` — one validated token

Produced exactly once per operand slot, by the F-2 grammar and the F-6 check pipeline. This is also where canonicalisation happens, so no downstream model ever observes leading zeros or a `-0`.

| Field | Type | Card. | Constraints | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | int | 1 | `1` for `raw_args[0]`, `2` for `raw_args[1]`; 1-based, positional | `FR-26` |
| `raw` | str | 1 | Verbatim token; **immutable** for the lifetime of the run | `FR-7`, safe echo |
| `accepted` | bool | 1 | `True` iff `raw` matches `DM-2.pattern` and violates no forbidden rule | `FR-27`–`FR-32` |
| `sign` | enum `{IMPLICIT_POSITIVE, POSITIVE, NEGATIVE}` | 0..1 | Present iff `accepted` | `FR-29`, `FR-30` |
| `magnitude_digits` | str | 0..1 | Present iff `accepted`; **canonical** digit string (see Conventions) | `FR-28`, `FR-79` |
| `value` | int | 0..1 | Present iff `accepted`; exact arbitrary precision, sign applied | `FR-52`, `FR-53` |
| `is_zero` | bool | 0..1 | Present iff `accepted`; `True` iff `value == 0` | `FR-54` |
| `rejected_by` | str | 0..1 | Present iff `not accepted`; names the violated grammar rule | `FR-31`, `FR-32` |

**Invariants**

- `accepted == (rejected_by == None)` and `not accepted == (value == None)`.
- `accepted` ⟹ `value == (1 if sign != NEGATIVE else -1) * int(magnitude_digits)`.
- **Zero canonicalisation:** `raw ∈ {"0", "+0", "-0", "00", "-000", "+00042"}` maps to `sign == IMPLICIT_POSITIVE`, `magnitude_digits == "0"`, `value == 0`, `is_zero == True`. The textual form of the input is never propagated to the result.
- `magnitude_digits` is canonical ⟹ it carries no leading zeros, so `DM-4` and `DM-5` cannot inherit any.
- `raw` is never mutated, trimmed, or rewritten — it exists solely so `DM-6` can echo the offending token safely.
- No floating-point or `Decimal` value is ever constructed for `value` (`FR-53`).

### DM-4: `Sum` — the arithmetic result

Owned by F-3 / F-8 / F-9. Holds the exact sum plus the derived attributes the renderer needs, so the renderer performs no arithmetic of its own.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | int | Exact `int1 + int2`; arbitrary precision; never overflows, truncates, rounds, saturates, or wraps | `FR-51`, `FR-52` |
| `is_negative` | bool | `True` iff `value < 0` | `FR-176` |
| `is_zero` | bool | `True` iff `value == 0` | `FR-54`, `FR-55` |
| `magnitude_digits` | str | Canonical base-10 digits of `abs(value)`; `"0"` when zero | `FR-79`, `FR-202` |
| `digit_count` | int | `1` when `value == 0`, else `len(magnitude_digits)` | `FR-202` |

**Invariants**

- `value == operands[1].value + operands[2].value`.
- Sign rules (`FR-54`): same-sign operands ⟹ `sign(value)` equals that sign and `magnitude_digits` is the digit-wise sum of magnitudes; opposite-sign operands ⟹ `magnitude_digits` is the digit-wise difference of magnitudes and `sign(value)` follows the larger magnitude; equal magnitudes ⟹ `value == 0`, `magnitude_digits == "0"`, `is_negative == False`.
- Additive identity: if either operand is `0`, `value` equals the other operand exactly (`FR-55`).
- Exactly one of `is_negative` / `is_zero` is ever true; they are never both true.
- `len(magnitude_digits) == digit_count` and `digit_count >= 1`.
- No fixed-width bound: `digit_count` is limited only by available process memory (`FR-201`). There is no 16/19/32/64/128-bit cap anywhere in this model.
- `magnitude_digits` contains only `U+0030`–`U+0039`; the sign is **not** part of this field (it is carried by `is_negative`), so sign and digits cannot be encoded twice.

### DM-5: `OutputEnvelope` — the stdout record

Owned by F-4 (and constrained by F-8, F-9). This is the only model permitted to touch stdout.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream` | enum `{STDOUT}` | Fixed; this model cannot address stderr | `FR-4`, `FR-76` |
| `payload` | str | `("-" if sum.is_negative else "") + sum.magnitude_digits` | `FR-77`, `FR-176` |
| `encoding` | enum `{ASCII}` | `payload` bytes are ASCII; UTF-8-compatible as a strict subset | `FR-77`, `FR-177` |
| `terminator` | `U+000A` | Exactly one; `U+000D` CR is never emitted | `FR-78` |
| `byte_length` | int | `len(payload.encode("ascii")) + 1` | `FR-78` |
| `trailing_bytes` | `[]` | Always empty; nothing may follow the terminator | `FR-78` |

**Invariants**

- Present iff `Invocation.outcome == SUCCESS`; absent on **every** failure path — this is the zero-stdout-bytes guarantee of `FR-127`.
- `payload` contains no leading zeros (`sum.magnitude_digits` is canonical), no thousands separator, no radix prefix, no exponent, no ANSI escape, no Unicode digit glyph.
- Sign, when present, is exactly one leading ASCII `-` U+002D byte `0x2D`; U+2212 and any other minus-like glyph are forbidden (`FR-177`).
- Exactly one write of exactly `byte_length` bytes; then the stream is flushed and never written again.
- Deterministic: identical `Sum` ⟹ byte-identical `OutputEnvelope`, on every machine and locale.

### DM-6: `DiagnosticMessage` — the stderr record (F-6)

| Field | Type | Card. | Constraints | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | enum `{ARITY_ERROR, GRAMMAR_ERROR}` | 1 | Determines which catalogue entry is used | `FR-126`, `FR-127` |
| `error_line` | str | 1 | Single line; contains **no** embedded `\n`; ASCII only | `FR-127` |
| `offending_slot` | int | 0..1 | `1` or `2`; present for `GRAMMAR_ERROR` only | `FR-7` |
| `offending_raw` | str | 0..1 | Safe echo of the verbatim violating token; present for `GRAMMAR_ERROR` only | `FR-7` |
| `usage_ref` | `DM-8` | 0..1 | Present for `ARITY_ERROR` (second stderr line) | `FR-226` |
| `stream` | enum `{STDERR}` | 1 | Cannot address stdout | `FR-6`, `FR-7` |
| `terminator` | `U+000A` | 1 | One per emitted line | `FR-127` |

**Invariants**

- At most one `GRAMMAR_ERROR` per run (the pipeline aborts at the first failing stage — `FR-126`); exactly one `ARITY_ERROR` if arity fails.
- `ARITY_ERROR` ⟹ exactly two stderr lines (error line + usage line); `GRAMMAR_ERROR` ⟹ exactly one stderr line.
- Message text is fixed and deterministic; the only interpolation is the safe echo of `offending_raw`. No locale translation, no timestamp, no hostname, no PID, no runtime-varying content (`FR-10` surface).
- Echoing must not re-interpret: control characters, non-ASCII bytes, or shell metacharacters in `offending_raw` must not be able to corrupt the diagnostic or inject additional lines. `offending_raw` is bounded to a single line.
- Never emitted on stdout; never emitted on a successful run.

### DM-7: `ExitStatus` — terminal status (constant enum)

| Member | Value | Condition | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SUCCESS` | `0` | Exactly two operands, both accepted, result line fully written to stdout | `FR-101`, `FR-5` |
| `USAGE_ERROR` | `2` | Arity failure **or** any operand failing the F-2 grammar; nothing written to stdout | `FR-102`, `FR-103` |

**Invariants**

- Exactly one status per process; set once, at termination, and never revised.
- `stdout_record` present ⟺ `USAGE_ERROR` not selected; `diagnostics` non-empty ⟺ `USAGE_ERROR` selected.
- No other value is ever returned on a spec-covered path. Uncaught internal faults are out of spec and are not modelled here.

### DM-8: `UsageText` — the usage literal (constant)

| Field | Type | Constraints | Owning FRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `literal` | str | Fixed ASCII text naming the `add <int1> <int2>` invocation; single line | `FR-226` |
| `terminator` | `U+000A` | Exactly one | `FR-226` |
| `stream` | enum `{STDERR}` | Never stdout | `FR-226` |
| `emission_count` | int | At most `1` per run | `FR-226` |
| `interpolations` | `[]` | Always empty — no program name, no version, no runtime values substituted | `FR-226` |
| `localized` | `false` | Not translated under any locale | F-10 boundary |

**Invariants**

- Byte-identical across runs, hosts, interpreters, time zones, and locales.
- Not reachable via any flag: there is no `--help`/`-h` path (`FR-26`, no option parsing). The usage surface is reachable only as part of a failing invocation.
- Never co-emitted with a successful `OutputEnvelope`.

### DM-9: `TestCase` — one verification fixture (F-11)

Owned by F-11. Exists only inside the test process; never shipped as runtime data.

| Field | Type | Card. | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_id` | str | 1 | Stable, unique within the suite |
| `target` | enum `{FUNCTION, CLI}` | 1 | `FUNCTION` exercises the internal adder directly; `CLI` exercises the process surface |
| `argv` | str[] | 0..* | Required for `CLI`; `argv[0]` is the program name and is not an operand |
| `operands` | (int, int) | 0..1 | Required for `FUNCTION` |
| `expected_stdout` | bytes | 1 | Literal expected bytes, including terminator |
| `expected_stderr` | bytes \| matcher | 0..1 | Literal bytes or a documented matcher for the F-6 catalogue |
| `expected_exit_status` | int | 0..1 | Required for `CLI`; one of `DM-7`'s values |
| `category` | enum `{HAPPY_PATH, ARITY, GRAMMAR, SIGN, PRECISION, STREAM_HYGIENE}` | 1 | Drives coverage accounting |
| `covers` | str[] | 1..* | Plain-text references to the FR ids under test |

**Invariants**

- Expected values are **literals**, never recomputed via the code under test — a test must not be able to pass by reproducing the bug.
- Every `TC`-level fixture uses only the Python 3 standard library and requires no network, no install step, and no build step.
- Categories `ARITY`, `GRAMMAR`, `SIGN`, `PRECISION`, `STREAM_HYGIENE` each contain at least one fixture; `PRECISION` includes at least one case whose operands exceed any fixed machine word (e.g. operands of ≥ 1,000 digits) to pin `FR-201`/`FR-202`.

### DM-10: `TestResult` — one executed fixture outcome (F-11)

| Field | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `test_id` | str | Foreign key to `DM-9.test_id` |
| `status` | enum `{PASS, FAIL, ERROR, SKIP}` | `ERROR` = the harness itself raised; `SKIP` must be `0` on a conforming run |
| `observed_stdout` | bytes | Verbatim captured stdout |
| `observed_stderr` | bytes | Verbatim captured stderr |
| `observed_exit_status` | int \| null | Null for `FUNCTION` targets |
| `diff_note` | str | 0..1; human-readable mismatch explanation on `FAIL`/`ERROR` |

**Invariants**

- Comparison is **byte-exact** on stdout and exit status; stderr is byte-exact for `ARITY`/`GRAMMAR` fixtures.
- `status == PASS` requires all three of stdout, stderr, and exit status to match their expectations where specified.
- A `FUNCTION`-target result never asserts on exit status (no process was spawned).

### DM-11: `TestSuite` — the aggregate run (F-11)

| Field | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `cases` | `TestCase[]` | Non-empty; ids unique |
| `results` | `TestResult[]` | `len(results) == len(cases)` on a completed run |
| `runner_command` | str | Exactly `python -m unittest` (or `python -m unittest discover`) from the project root |
| `third_party_deps` | `[]` | Always empty |
| `network_required` | `bool` | Always `False` |
| `install_step_required` | `bool` | Always `False` |
| `summary_status` | enum `{PASS, FAIL}` | `PASS` iff every result is `PASS` |

**Invariants**

- Deterministic and repeatable: two consecutive runs on the same interpreter produce identical `results` statuses.
- No test writes to the project tree, no test requires a specific CWD other than the project root, no test depends on wall-clock time, hostname, or locale.

### Relationships

```
Invocation (DM-1)
 ├── raw_args ─────────────► [str]  (positional, unmodified)
 ├── validates against ────► DecimalIntegerGrammar (DM-2)  [constant]
 ├── operands ─────────────► ParsedOperand (DM-3) ×2
 ├── computes ─────────────► Sum (DM-4)
 ├── renders ──────────────► OutputEnvelope (DM-5)   ──► stdout   (success only)
 ├── diagnostics ──────────► DiagnosticMessage (DM-6) ──► stderr   (failure only)
 │                              └── usage_ref ──► UsageText (DM-8) [constant]
 └── terminates with ──────► ExitStatus (DM-7)        [constant enum]

TestSuite (DM-11) ── contains ──► TestCase (DM-9) ── produces ──► TestResult (DM-10)
                                   └── exercises ──► DM-1 (CLI target) or DM-4/DM-3 (FUNCTION target)
```

Cardinality summary: `Invocation 1 ── 0..2 ParsedOperand`; `Invocation 1 ── 0..1 Sum`; `Sum 1 ── 0..1 OutputEnvelope`; `Invocation 1 ── 0..* DiagnosticMessage`; `TestSuite 1 ── 1..* TestCase 1 ── 0..1 TestResult`.

| Model | Lifetime | Mutability | Persisted? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DM-2` Grammar | Process | Immutable constant | No |
| `DM-7` ExitStatus | Process | Immutable constant | No |
| `DM-8` UsageText | Process | Immutable constant | No |
| `DM-1` Invocation | One run | Write-once per field, terminal after `exit_status` | No |
| `DM-3` ParsedOperand | One run | Write-once; `raw` never mutated | No |
| `DM-4` Sum | One run | Write-once | No |
| `DM-5` OutputEnvelope | One run | Write-once, then emitted once | No |
| `DM-6` DiagnosticMessage | One run | Write-once, then emitted once | No |
| `DM-9`–`DM-11` Test models | Test process only | Fixtures immutable; results append-only | No |

### Cross-cutting data invariants

- **No floating point anywhere.** No model in this section may be represented with binary or decimal floating-point types at any point in its lifetime (`FR-53`).
- **No locale dependence.** Digit rendering, sign encoding, sorting, and diagnostic text are all locale-invariant; no model reads `LANG`/`LC_*` or any formatting locale (`FR-77`, `FR-177`).
- **No fixed width.** No model carries an implicit 32/64/128-bit bound; precision is limited only by memory (`FR-201`).
- **ASCII-clean machine output.** Every byte reaching stdout is ASCII; diagnostics and usage text are ASCII as well.
- **Stream purity.** Only `DM-5` may address stdout; only `DM-6` and `DM-8` may address stderr; no model may address both.
- **Determinism.** For any fixed argument vector, the tuple (`DM-5` bytes, `DM-6`/`DM-8` bytes, `DM-7` value) is byte-identical on every run, host, interpreter, and locale.
